page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ic5.8xlarge is a compute-heavy x86_64 server powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The system provides 16 physical cores yielding 32 virtual CPUs through hyperthreading, accompanied by 32 KB L1d cache per core, 1.0 MB L2 cache per core, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache. It incorporates 32.0 GB of memory, establishing a 1:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio of 1.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include local NVMe storage or discrete GPUs, relying on remote block storage and dedicated networking capped at a 10 Gbps baseline throughput. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AES, BMI2, and FMA.

Benchmark results reveal a contrast between single-threaded execution and multi-core throughput. Single-core tests fall into the lower performance quartile, with stress-ng single-core scoring 1106.89 and single-threaded gzip compression registering 19.05 GB/sec. However, full core utilization scales effectively, pushing multi-core performance metrics like stress-ng multi-core (23616.79) and Geekbench multi-core (8847.0) into average performance tiers. Memory performance remains stable with uncached read speeds reaching 95.0 GB/sec and write speeds at 45.75 GB/sec. From a hardware density perspective, the high vCPU count relative to memory capacity offers targeted compute capacity for parallelized execution where memory consumption per thread is low.

Due to the minimal 1.0 GB RAM allocation per vCPU, the ecs.ic5.8xlarge instance is suited for highly parallelized, compute-bound tasks with tight memory footprints. Appropriate workloads include parallel software compilation (Geekbench compiling score 18175.0), multithreaded decompression tasks, batch compute pipelines, static web serving (17.02 GB/sec throughput), and lightweight key-value processing such as Redis SET operations (22.46 million ops/sec). It also supports lightweight LLM inference on small models (1408.87 tokens/sec prompt processing on 135M models), though memory limits preclude execution of large-parameter models.
